profile.headline: Software Engineer Intern @ Etogy | Building AI Payment Solutions | Rust · Python
profile.summary:
I got into engineering because I couldn't stop asking how things work, and I don't really know something until I build it myself. That's why I've written a PostgreSQL client in Rust for Python to cut the C dependency, and a package manager for the WebAssembly Component Model.

That curiosity is how a TA role at Ensign College's IT department grew into the university's first SRE practice. What started as grading and emails became production K3s clusters serving 1,000+ users, a Kafka pipeline pushing 30M+ messages/day, observability across 50+ Proxmox servers, and a 74% cut in AWS costs,  infrastructure the department's developers and students rely on daily.

Now I'm going a level deeper into the systems most people never see: at Etogy, a fintech, I work on the AI and Federal Reserve team, where our code moves ACH payments between the Fed and partner banks. I've deployed and benchmarked LLMs across GPUs with tensor parallelism, proposed serving architectures, and built MCP integrations connecting models to our payment processor.

Every shift in my work has been the same move: build the thing, then understand what it runs on, then build the layer underneath for the people downstream. Payments turned out to be the best version of that: regulated, unforgiving, and full of infrastructure that has to be boring in the best way.

C# / .NET · Python · Rust · LLM Inference · MCP · Kubernetes · Kafka · PostgreSQL · Terraform · AWS · Docker · ArgoCD · WebAssembly/WASI · Linux

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
AI and Federal Reserve team at a fintech, the code moves ACH payments between the Fed and partner banks.
- Shipped the retrieval layer of a production MCP server now used in enterprise sales demos, building semantic search over 200 API documentation nodes in Qdrant with colbert-ir/colbertv2.0 embeddings.
- Kept the RAG service available under GPU saturation by owning an adaptive degradation controller that reads 7 live signals and tiers sessions down to CPU embeddings, built on Netflix's load-shedding pattern.
- Selected the production serving model by benchmarking 9 LLMs across 4 accelerator configurations and 2 inference engines (vLLM, llama.cpp) against a gpt-oss-120b baseline, then validating the finalist with guidellm.
- Eliminated 8 of 9 candidate models before deployment by running adversarial robustness evaluations against chain-of-thought injection and system-prompt extraction.
- Deployed and benchmarked LLMs across GPUs with tensor parallelism and proposed the serving architecture.
- Delivered Federal Reserve payment integrations (FedACH) in C#/.NET, implementing NACHA file handling, effective-date arithmetic, and Fed holiday calendar logic.
- Cut merchant-risk screening from ~90 minutes to 25 seconds across 50K+ merchant records by rewriting the service around an Aho-Corasick-inspired prescreen with regex verification.
- Reduced false positives from 3–4 every two days to near zero. Surfacing a confirmed fraud case by adding an n-gram prescreen with narrowed fuzzy matching.
- Reviewed pull requests spanning retrieval, agent orchestration, and SQL Server CTEs and stored procedures.

projects.title: Oxpg
projects.description:
A PostgreSQL client for Python, written in Rust with PyO3 on top of tokio-postgres. Most Python Postgres libraries depend on libpq (a C library) under the hood. Oxpg wraps an async Rust implementation instead, keeping the entire stack C-free. The motivation was WASI compatibility: C dependencies block Python database code from running in WebAssembly environments. Still evolving, but the core works.

Rust · PyO3 · tokio-postgres · PostgreSQL · Python
